# Every test case in the pinned aws-guard-rules-registry corpus whose rule ran and did not meet its
# expectation, as `cfn-guard test -d` reports it with this evaluator. One line per (case, rule), in the
# shape .github/scripts/check-registry-corpus.sh builds from the report's `failed_rules` entries:
# `  <case name>: rule <rule name>, expected <expectation>, evaluated <verdict>`. The two leading
# spaces are part of the line.
#
# Listed here because a failed rule moves nothing the exit code can carry. The corpus already has
# unchecked expectations, which pin the exit code at 1, so a rule that runs and fails its expectation
# changes the number not at all -- see condition 3 of the script. Read this list as a lock on a known
# state: a line appearing here is a rule that newly fails its expectation and turns the job red, and a
# line disappearing means the evaluator or the corpus moved and this file has to say so.
#
# Both lines are the "No Method set in API GW Stage, SKIP" case of two API Gateway rules. That test
# input is malformed: its `Resources:` holds `Type` and `Properties` directly instead of a map of
# resources, so `Resources.*[ Type == 'AWS::ApiGateway::Stage' ... ]` walks a string and a map that
# are not resources. Earlier releases deselected both in silence and reported SKIP; this evaluator
# refuses the read the predicate cannot decide, and a rule-level `when` meeting a refusal fails the
# rule rather than reporting it not applicable, so the case evaluates FAIL. The registry's own main
# carries the same input, so aws-cloudformation/aws-guard-rules-registry#288 does not clear these.

  No Method set in API GW Stage, SKIP: rule API_GW_CACHE_ENABLED_AND_ENCRYPTED, expected SKIP, evaluated FAIL
  No Method set in API GW Stage, SKIP: rule API_GW_EXECUTION_LOGGING_ENABLED, expected SKIP, evaluated FAIL
